cards.explanation: The answer is the land of Israel. Ezekiel is living in exile, far from home, and then "In visions of God He took me to the land of Israel…" (Ezekiel 40:2). He doesn't just visit the land, either. The LORD sets him on a very high mountain. I spent years stuck in a drawer, so I know what it's like to get carried somewhere better.

The man in the gateway is holding a linen cord and a measuring rod. He was "…standing in the gateway with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand." (Ezekiel 40:3). Those are measuring tools, friends. Right away that tells you he's here to measure something. My own measuring tools are a scoop and a squint, so I respect the upgrade.

The answer is to see everything the man will show him. The man says, "…pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here." (Ezekiel 40:4). Ezekiel's job is to look and listen closely. When the whole trip is about seeing, you'd better not blink.

The answer is False. The man doesn't tell Ezekiel to keep it to himself. He says, "Report to the house of Israel everything you see." (Ezekiel 40:4). So Ezekiel is told to share it, friends. Keeping it to himself is the opposite of what the man says.
The answer is east. "Then he came to the gate facing east and climbed its steps." (Ezekiel 40:6). That's the first gate the man measures. After that comes the threshold, which is one rod deep.

The answer is that the man brings Ezekiel into the outer court. "Then he brought me into the outer court…" (Ezekiel 40:17). Ezekiel just watched a whole east gate get measured, and now he's led inside to chambers and a pavement laid out all around, with thirty chambers facing the pavement. I think Ezekiel's feet need a nap by now. That man has a rod in his hand and ground to cover.

The answer is the south gate. "Next he brought me into the inner court through the south gate…" (Ezekiel 40:28). Then the man measures it, and it matches the others. Measure, match, repeat. I wish every batch I'd stamped had come out that consistent.

The word is burnt. "There the burnt offering was to be washed." (Ezekiel 40:38). That happens in a chamber with a doorway by the portico in each inner gateway. Even in a vision, somebody has to think about the cleanup, friends. I know that feeling, because a bakery has plenty of dishes too.

The tables inside the portico were for slaughtering the offerings. They are tables "…on which the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were to be slaughtered." (Ezekiel 40:39). So these are working tables. They're set inside the portico of the gateway, two on each side.

The answer is the temple. The man says, "The chamber that faces south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple…" (Ezekiel 40:45). So the south-facing chamber goes with the temple, friends. The next verse gives the other chamber its own job.

The answer is True. The man says, "…the chamber that faces north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar." (Ezekiel 40:46). The south-facing chamber is for the priests who keep charge of the temple (Ezekiel 40:45). Two chambers, two jobs.

The answer is that only the sons of Zadok may approach the LORD to minister. The man says, "These are the sons of Zadok, the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him." (Ezekiel 40:46). Look at who's getting set apart here: not all the Levites, just Zadok's sons. He says it right after pointing out two chambers in the inner court, one for the priests who keep charge of the temple and one for the priests who keep charge of the altar.
